title: Fish, salmon, baked or broiled, coated

content.title: About
content.content: Salmon is a marine fish from the Salmonidae family, prized for its delicate flavor and high content of healthy fats. When baked or broiled with a coating, it stays juicy while the crispy crust adds a pleasant texture contrast.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Salmon can migrate between the ocean and freshwater rivers where they spawn.
Coatings are often made from whole grains, spices, and a small amount of oil, enhancing aroma and crunch.
Baking retains more omega‑3 fatty acids than deep‑frying in oil.
In Japan, salmon is sometimes served as “sabai,” lightly seared and brushed with soy sauce.
Salmon is called the “king of fish” because of its high vitamin D content.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Omega‑3s support heart health, reduce inflammation, and aid brain function.

items.title: High-quality protein
items.content: Salmon provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12 and B6 help form red blood cells and maintain nervous system health.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Regulates calcium levels and supports the immune system.

items.title: Selenium
items.content: An antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including salmon.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: While salmon generally has low mercury, pregnant women and children should limit intake.

items.title: High‑salt coating
items.content: Overly salty coatings can raise blood pressure; choose low‑sodium options when possible.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Coating and oil increase the dish’s calories, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Coated salmon can be served as a main dish with vegetable sides, mashed potatoes, or a fresh salad. It also works well sliced for sandwiches, salads, or tossed with pasta.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared product refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 63 °C before serving.
